title: Board of Appeals members: dissents, and motions that fail
question: How often does each member of the Board of Appeals dissent, and how often does a motion fail for lack of votes so that the department’s decision stands?
finding: The minutes record 293 votes with a printed tally (September 2022 to November 2026); 34 (11.6%) had a dissent, and members’ dissent shares run from 1.3% (Jose Lopez, 235 votes) to 4.3% (Rebecca Saroyan, 69). A motion failed for lack of votes in 7 appeals and in 6 of 45 requests for a rehearing or late filing, and 5 appeals ended with the department’s decision standing by default.
how: Each action paragraph with a printed tally counts once, even where several appeals were heard together. A member is counted as voting when listed as present and not named as absent or recused; a dissent is counted when the minutes name the member as dissenting. “Failed for lack of votes” is read from the action text. Members with fewer than 20 votes are left out; spellings of one member’s name are merged.
limits: The minutes never list more than 5 members present, and they show motions failing for want of a set number of votes, so with a member absent or a seat empty a decision can stand even when most of those present voted to change it. A dissent shows a difference of view on one case and nothing else. Members sat in different years and heard different cases. Recusals are those the minutes print. A difference between areas, or between groups of cases, is not proof of bias. Areas differ in what is proposed, in zoning, lot sizes, building ages and land prices, and in who chooses to apply, object or appeal at all.

sources.t: San Francisco Board of Appeals, hearing minutes, September 2022 to November 2026 (one set shown)
San Francisco Board of Appeals, Case Report of November 12, 2026
